correctness.rationale: For n>=5 and independent uniform circle points, the inscribed-angle theorem gives vertex i acute iff G_(i-1)+G_i>1/2. A labelled adjacent-pair sum S is Beta(2,n-2); the split U=A/S is independent Uniform(0,1). Exact survival (1-s)^(n-2)(1+(n-2)s) gives n(S-1/2)|S>1/2 ⇒ Exp(rate 2). The known Putnam multiple-acute conditional probability 2/(n-2) vanishes, so selecting a unique acute vertex preserves the limit. Residual Dirichlet gaps have maximum tending to 0, yielding Hausdorff convergence of the remaining vertices to a complementary semicircle. The limiting semicircular hull plus one apex has area π/2+sin(πU), perimeter π+2(sin(πU/2)+cos(πU/2)); the area CDF and expected limits follow by change of variables and bounded convergence. Independently derived Beta tail expansion and marked arc geometry. The sampler only corroborates finite n, not the asymptotic proof.
